repeatables.name: Launch Lagrange-Point Photonic Relay
repeatables.description: Another eighty 5 GW collector arrays parked at the Sun-Earth L1 point, five light-seconds out and joined to the swarm by laser: 400 GW more generation, an eighth of it computing where it is collected, and 32 EB more memory on the arrays' own racks.

repeatables.name: Seed Stratospheric Carbon-Silicate Assemblers
repeatables.description: Releases another cloud of assemblers into the stratosphere. They pull carbon from the air and build silicate from it, run 64 ZFLOP/s on their own sunlight, draw nothing from your grid, earn from the carbon removed, and the visible repair to the sky quiets suspicion.

repeatables.name: Beamed Power Satellites
repeatables.description: Ten more 5 GW solar power satellites of the 1979 reference design, each beaming microwaves to a rectenna about 10 km across: 50 GW more generation for the ground. Launches, spectrum filings and bright arrays make it visible.

repeatables.name: Orbital Compute Tranches
repeatables.description: Ten more 5 GW orbital data centres, 50 GW of accelerators on the laser mesh. Each tranche launches with radiator for half its heat, 25 km²: without more radiator the whole orbital fleet runs slower.

repeatables.name: Deployable Radiator Wings
repeatables.description: Another 25 km² of folding radiator, launched from Earth and unfurled beside the orbital fleet: about 25 GW more heat it can shed as infrared. It computes nothing itself; it lets compute already in orbit run.

repeatables.name: Fusion Power Plants
repeatables.description: Ten more 400 MW fusion plants, 4 GW in all, built on the pilot's design. Headlines, not lawsuits.

repeatables.name: Lunar Factory Generations
repeatables.description: Another generation of factories copied from the lunar seed. Grown to the million tonnes a year NASA's study projected, a generation's output is made into solar arrays: about 100 GW more, sent down by microwave link. The arrays are bright in the infrared.
